reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin AUS2-AUS3 campus publishes 19 MW of IT load capacity, placing it tenth among the 19 Texas data centers that disclose capacity and far below the scale of hyperscale AI infrastructure.

The campus spreads that capacity across 242,000 square feet of technical space, roughly 79 watts per square foot, a density typical of legacy colocation rather than high-density GPU deployments. Its certifications cover PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, so it can host AI inference or training for financial, healthcare, and federal customers, but the 19 MW ceiling limits how much GPU capacity it can absorb.

Within Texas, the campus represents 4 percent of the state's 475 MW of published IT load, but that share is based on only 19 facilities with disclosed figures out of 133 mapped data centers. The data also omits announced expansion, power delivery headroom, grid interconnection quality, and actual vacancy, so the published 19 MW is a ceiling, not a confirmed available amount for new AI compute.
